description: Canonical, human-readable JSON-Schema-style description of the Microsoft Secure Future Initiative (SFI) knowledge base. The synthesis step assembles the files below from the staging extracts; a Python loader and an MCP server rely on these shapes. Shapes are expressed with type strings ('string', 'integer', 'boolean', 'array<string>', 'array<object>'), nested objects for object fields, and inline enum notes. Every '*_url' field is a string URL; dates are ISO 8601 unless noted.

sfi_pillars.json.description: The six SFI engineering pillars with their Zero Trust mapping, NIST CSF functions, objectives, best practices, and audit criteria. This is the primary structured source; sfi_checklists.json is derived from every pillar's audit_criteria.

items.slug: string (enum: see conventions.slugs; one of the six pillar slugs)
items.name: string (human-readable pillar name)
items.statement: string (one-sentence description of the pillar's goal)

zero_trust.verify_explicitly: string (how the Verify explicitly principle applies to this pillar)
zero_trust.use_least_privilege: string (how the Use least privilege principle applies to this pillar)
zero_trust.assume_breach: string (how the Assume breach principle applies to this pillar)

items.nist_csf_detail: string (prose describing how the listed NIST functions/categories apply to this pillar)

items.zero_trust: string (the associated Zero Trust principle and how it applies, e.g. 'Assume breach: Treat build and repo systems as potential targets.')
items.adoption_considerations: string (trade-offs or effort involved in adopting the practice)

items.id: string (slug, unique within the pillar, e.g. 'require-code-approval')
items.how_to_verify: string (concrete steps or evidence to check)
items.signals: array<string> (positive indicators that the requirement is met, e.g. file names, config keys, tool names)
items.anti_signals: array<string> (indicators that the requirement is violated or absent)

sfi_principles.json.description: Cross-cutting glossaries shared by the whole knowledge base: SFI security principles, Zero Trust principles, NIST CSF 2.0 functions, and a short SFI overview. Produced from principles.json in staging.

shape._notes: string (optional; records fetch gaps, provenance, or extraction caveats)

sfi_patterns.json.description: Catalog of concrete security patterns and practices harvested from SFI progress reports, plus a per-report index. Each pattern is attributed to a pillar and to the report it came from.

items.title: string (name of the pattern or practice)
items.url: string (url to the pattern's source or guidance)
items.source_report: string (name/date of the SFI progress report the pattern came from, e.g. 'SFI progress report - July 2026')

items.name: string (report name, e.g. 'SFI progress report')
items.new_patterns: array<string> (titles of patterns introduced in this report; should correspond to patterns[].title)

sfi_checklists.json.description: A flattened, scanner-ready view derived from every pillar's audit_criteria in sfi_pillars.json. Each checklist item is denormalized with its owning pillar so a scanner can iterate a single flat list without walking the pillar tree.

items.id: string (globally unique; typically '<pillar_slug>/<audit_criteria.id>' or the pillar's audit_criteria id)
items.requirement: string (copied from the source audit criterion)

sources.json.description: Provenance ledger of every source consulted while building the knowledge base, including whether the fetch returned readable content and what KB content it informed.

items.title: string
items.readable: boolean (true if the fetch returned usable content, false if blocked/empty/JS-only)
items.used_for: string (what KB content this source informed, e.g. 'pillar 4 objectives')
items.report_version: string|null (SFI report version/date if the source is a progress report, else null)
